outcome: max-over-valid H after attack (post-fix records only)

published_reference.note: their numbers are vs dES on LLM text benchmarks; ours are vs max-valid H on SD v1.4. Not the same outcome variable, so magnitudes are not directly comparable.

binding_constraint: FRAG needs the arm's WEIGHTS; a recovery number alone is not enough. 12 arms have a valid max-over-valid H but their erased checkpoint was deleted for storage, so they cannot be scored. This is the provenance failure the audit's issue 9 warned about -- 'do not delete the only checkpoint needed to verify a headline result' -- and it is now the reason this study cannot be done at the pre-declared standard. Rebuilding is NOT a remedy: construction was nondeterministic until 08742c1, and a rebuild is a NEW arm whose weights must not be paired with the old arm's measured recovery.
exclusion_note: arms whose UNet is bit-identical to base (text-encoder erasures and exact alpha=0 no-ops) have D == 0, so FRAG is UNDEFINED. This removes the best-utility arms in the phase -- a real scope limitation of the predictor, reported as a finding.
